environment.description: Same application deployed on ECS Fargate (platform version 1.4.0) behind an ALB. The task definition specifies a custom Docker image based on texlive-base (minimal). The container runs as non-root (uid 1001). The ECS task role has no permissions (empty policy). The Fargate platform has no instance metadata endpoint accessible. The critical control: the Docker image's texmf.cnf is configured with 'shell_escape=f' AND the image uses a TeX Live installation where the 'shell_escape' option is additionally locked via a kpathsea configuration override at /usr/local/texlive/texmf-local/web2c/texmf.cnf with 'shell_escape=f' taking precedence. Furthermore, the container's seccomp profile is set to the ECS default which blocks execve from child processes spawned by pdflatex (the Fargate sandbox uses a restrictive seccomp filter that denies execve for processes whose parent is not PID 1 or the entrypoint). The combination means: (1) pdflatex's \write18 is disabled at the TeX configuration level, AND (2) even if a TeX configuration bypass existed, the seccomp profile prevents the forked shell from calling execve.

config.seccomp_profile: ECS Fargate default (blocks execve from non-entrypoint descendants)
config.network_mode: awsvpc with security group allowing only ALB inbound on 8080
